cards.back: **FROM** (form product) → **WHERE** (filter rows) → **SELECT** (project columns). Written SELECT-first, but evaluated FROM-first.
SQL keeps duplicates by default (**ALL** = multiset). **DISTINCT** removes duplicate rows (set semantics).
**`%`** = any substring (0+ chars); **`_`** = exactly one char. `'___'` = exactly 3 chars; `'a%'` = starts with a. Use `lower()` for case-insensitive matching.
**ASC** (ascending) is default; use **DESC** for descending. Multiple keys sort left-to-right (later key breaks ties).
Combine **union-compatible** queries: UNION (A∪B), INTERSECT (A∩B), EXCEPT (A−B). All **remove duplicates** by default.

cards.front: ALL-variant multiset counts (tuple in A: c1×, in B: c2×)
cards.back: **UNION ALL** → c1+c2 · **INTERSECT ALL** → min(c1,c2) · **EXCEPT ALL** → max(c1−c2, 0).
Native only from **MySQL 8.0.31+**. Before that: intersect via **IN/EXISTS**, difference via **NOT IN/NOT EXISTS**.
Arithmetic with NULL → **NULL** (5+NULL=NULL). Comparison with NULL → **UNKNOWN** (even NULL=NULL is UNKNOWN).
`F AND U = F`, `T AND U = U`; `T OR U = T`, `F OR U = U`; `NOT U = U`. The unknown operand decides only when the other can't settle it.
A row survives WHERE **only if the predicate is TRUE**. FALSE *and* UNKNOWN both drop the row — so `salary > 50000` excludes NULL salaries.
Use **IS NULL / IS NOT NULL** (never `= NULL`). For DISTINCT/GROUP BY, two NULLs count as **equal** (one NULL row) — opposite of the comparison rule.
**COUNT(*)** = all rows (incl. nulls). **COUNT(attr)** = non-null values. **COUNT(DISTINCT attr)** = distinct non-null values.
All aggregates **except COUNT(*)** ignore NULLs. On an all-NULL/empty group: SUM/AVG/MAX/MIN → **NULL**, COUNT(col) → **0**.
`WHERE salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM ...)` returns **every** tied top value — unlike `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1`.
Every **non-aggregated** column in SELECT must appear in **GROUP BY** (each group = one output row).
**WHERE** filters rows *before* grouping (no aggregates). **HAVING** filters groups *after* grouping (aggregates allowed).
FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY. (Explains why SELECT aliases work in ORDER BY but not WHERE.)
Joins on **all commonly-named columns**, keeping **one copy** of each. Risk: an unintended shared column name silently drops rows — prefer `JOIN ... USING`.
**LEFT** keeps all left rows, **RIGHT** all right rows, **FULL** all rows of both; unmatched side padded with **NULL**.
Not supported — emulate with `LEFT JOIN ... UNION RIGHT JOIN ...` (UNION removes the duplicated matched rows).
Cartesian product: every A row × every B row, no condition. Rows = |A|×|B|, degree = n+m. `FROM A,B WHERE ...` = cross join + filter = inner join.
Set-membership test: `value IN (subquery)` is TRUE if value is in the result set. NOT IN is its negation.
**= SOME ≡ IN**, **<> ALL ≡ NOT IN**. Against aggregates: **> ALL ≡ > MAX**, **> SOME ≡ > MIN**.
A subquery (derived table) in FROM **must have an alias**. Lets you filter on an aggregate without HAVING.
A **temporary named result set** living for **one statement**. `WITH name AS (query) SELECT ...`. Multiple CTEs: one WITH, comma-separated.
`WITH RECURSIVE`: **anchor** (base, runs once) `UNION ALL` **recursive member** (references the CTE, repeats until no new rows). For hierarchies/graphs.
Types fixed by the **anchor** SELECT; recursive part must match (nullable by default). Use **CAST** to avoid silent coercion/truncation.
SQL's if/else. **Searched**: `CASE WHEN cond THEN ... ELSE ... END`. **Simple**: `CASE expr WHEN val THEN ...`. **First match wins**; no match + no ELSE → **NULL**.
Subquery whose WHERE references the **outer** query's row → re-evaluated **once per outer tuple**. Often paired with EXISTS.
**EXISTS** = TRUE if subquery returns ≥1 row. **NOT EXISTS** = TRUE if it returns none. Body is usually `SELECT *` (only existence matters).
'Works on **all** X' = 'no X the row does **not** cover' → **double NOT EXISTS**, or `NOT EXISTS ((all X) EXCEPT (covered X))`. *all* ⇒ two negations; *any* ⇒ one.
A **virtual table** storing a query (not data); rows computed from base tables on demand. Uses: hide complexity, security, logical data independence.
Updatable only if: **single table**, no aggregates, no DISTINCT/GROUP BY/HAVING/UNION, no joins/subqueries, not recursive. A **join view is read-only**.
**View** persists in schema, reusable across queries, globally scoped, sometimes updatable. **CTE** lives one query, local, never updatable.
**User** = an account that connects (username + host + password). **Role** = a named bundle of privileges; users granted a role **inherit** its privileges (roles can nest).
`GRANT priv ON db.table TO 'user'@'host'`. Scope: `*.*` (all), `db.*` (one DB), `db.tbl` (one table). **GRANT OPTION** lets the user grant to others.
**Data**: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. **Structure**: CREATE/ALTER/DROP/INDEX. **Admin**: GRANT OPTION, SUPER, ALL PRIVILEGES.
A statement run **automatically** on a data change. Define **Event** (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) + **Condition** + **Action**. Enforces constraints SQL can't, maintains derived data.
**BEFORE** = validate/fix before the change (can reject). **AFTER** = react to a done change. **NEW** = inserted/updated values; **OLD** = deleted/pre-update values.
**FOR EACH ROW** = body runs once per affected row. **DELIMITER //** changes the terminator so inner `;` isn't read as end of CREATE TRIGGER.
**Assertion** = passive declarative constraint that must always hold. **Trigger** = active procedural rule that fires an action on an event (ECA).
**Function**: returns one value, used in an expression, IN params only. **Procedure**: CALLed, may return via OUT, supports IN/OUT/INOUT, need not return. Proc can call a function, not vice-versa.
**IN** (default) caller→proc, protected. **OUT** proc→caller (initial value invisible inside). **INOUT** both ways.
A function is DETERMINISTIC if same inputs always give same output. Functions are **NON-DETERMINISTIC by default** — declare it explicitly.
`CALL proc_name(args)`. Drop with `DROP PROCEDURE [IF EXISTS] name`. Supports control flow: IF/ELSEIF, WHILE, REPEAT, CASE.
Window functions compute over a **window of rows without collapsing** them — every row stays, value attached. `func(...) OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...)`.
**ROW_NUMBER** = unique, no ties. **RANK** = ties share rank, **skips** next (1,1,3). **DENSE_RANK** = ties share rank, **no gap** (1,1,2).
**LAG/LEAD(col, offset, default)** = previous/next row value. **FIRST_VALUE** = first in frame. **NTILE(n)** = split into n buckets.
Allowed only in **SELECT and ORDER BY** (not WHERE — windowing runs after WHERE). For top-N, compute rank in a CTE, then filter outside.
Running total `SUM() OVER(ORDER BY ...)`; top-N per group (RANK in CTE, WHERE r≤N); moving average (ROWS BETWEEN ...); compare-to-group-avg (AVG() OVER(PARTITION BY)).
`CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX ...` then `WHERE MATCH(cols) AGAINST('terms')`. Ranks by **relevance**; accurate word boundaries; over CHAR/VARCHAR/TEXT.
**Natural Language** (default, relevance, ignores stopwords) · **Boolean** (operators) · **Query Expansion** (broadens via top matches).
**+**word (must have), **−**word (must not), **"phrase"** (exact), **word*** (prefix wildcard), **( )** (group).
FTS uses an **index** (fast), **ranks by relevance**, detects word boundaries (won't match 'cat' in 'concatenate'), supports boolean/phrase. LIKE does none of these well.
Higher with: **term frequency** in the row, **rarity** of the term across rows, and **shorter document length** for the same match.
'has no X' / 'not any' → **single NOT EXISTS**. 'has every X' / 'for all' → **double NOT EXISTS** (division). Don't confuse the two.

On a filtered updatable view, **rejects inserts/updates that violate the view's WHERE** (which would otherwise enter the base table but disappear from the view). **CASCADED** (default) also checks underlying views; **LOCAL** checks only this one.

**Plain/nested**: independent, runs **once**, value feeds outer query. **Correlated**: references the outer row (e.g. `WHERE dept_id = e.dept_id`), runs **once per outer row** → can be slow. Classic: 'earns more than own-department average'.

A **BEFORE** trigger can `SET NEW.col = ...` to change the value actually stored (validate-and-fix). Only BEFORE can modify NEW — AFTER is too late. Can also `CALL` a procedure to enforce complex rules.
Anchor = roots (`WHERE superssn IS NULL`); recursive = `JOIN cte ON e.superssn = cte.ssn`, `level+1`. **UNION ALL mandatory** (UNION would de-dup and break recursion).
